title: S014 3.3 Interpretation and representation of time values
parent_path: S014 3.3 Interpretation and representation of time values

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client acquires a lease for a network address for a fixed period of time (which may be infinite).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there is drift between the two clocks, the server may consider the lease expired before the client does.
actions: server marks lease as expired in its local database

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To compensate, the server may return a shorter lease duration to the client than the server commits to its local database of client information.
actions: server includes shorter lease duration value in outbound DHCP message to client
server stores longer lease duration in local client database
